conversation.content: Take Toyota’s Just-in-Time system—it doesn’t just reroute parts when a supplier fails; it maintains backup suppliers *and* local buffer stocks so production never halts. Or look at Unilever’s tea supply chain in Kenya: they train smallholder farmers on climate-resilient practices *and* use blockchain to track crop health in real time, preventing delays before they happen. Even Amazon’s warehouse network uses predictive AI to pre-position inventory near high-risk zones—so when a storm hits, customers don’t even notice the disruption. These aren’t about smoothing over failures—they’re about engineering them out of existence. True resilience means your system works so quietly and reliably that users never have to wonder if it’ll hold. And honestly, if your supply chain needs to “calm” people during a delay, you’ve already lost.

content.text: Key principle: when the human mind perceives a form, the whole has a reality of  its own, independent of the parts.
Proximity.  We tend to see objects that are visually close  together as belonging to part of a group.

This allowed the development of 8 Gestalt Laws of Grouping. Here we are  highlighting only the most relevant 5 for data presentation. You can read more  details about them on Wikipedia:  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gestalt psychology

- The "G" is split into two separate black shapes, illustrating "Segregação" (Segregation), with an arrow and label above it.

- The "T" at the end is also striped, reinforcing similarity.
- The overall arrangement of the letters and their styles is surrounded by arrows that connect the principles to the word "Unidade" (Unity), which is labeled on the right side of the image.
